assessment.subject: Machine Learning Reliability
assessment.question: Why can fitting a scaler or feature selector on the full dataset before the train-test split make evaluation misleading, and how should a pipeline prevent it?
rubric: test-set information must not influence fitting
fit preprocessing only on training data
apply the fitted transform to held-out data
use a pipeline to keep fitting inside validation folds

answers.label: strong
answers.text: If the scaler or selector is fitted before splitting, its parameters use the held-out samples, so information about the test distribution influences training and the reported score can be optimistic. Fit every learned preprocessing step only on each training fold, then use that fitted transform on validation or test data. A pipeline enforces that order during cross-validation.

answers.label: misconception
answers.text: Scaling leaks data because multiplication changes the labels. The safest fix is to fit the scaler separately on the test set so its values stay accurate.

answers.label: partial
answers.text: The test set should remain separate. Split first and use a pipeline, although I am not sure whether the transform itself must be fitted again inside every cross-validation fold.

assessment.subject: Linear Algebra: Eigenvalues
assessment.question: When is an n by n matrix diagonalizable, and how are the matrices S and Lambda constructed?
rubric: columns of S are those eigenvectors
Lambda has corresponding eigenvalues on its diagonal
A equals S Lambda S inverse

answers.label: strong
answers.text: An n by n matrix is diagonalizable when it has n linearly independent eigenvectors. Put those eigenvectors in the columns of S and put their corresponding eigenvalues in the same order down the diagonal of Lambda. Then A = S Lambda S^{-1}. Repeated eigenvalues are allowed if there are still enough independent eigenvectors.

answers.label: misconception
answers.text: Every square matrix is diagonalizable. S contains the eigenvalues and Lambda contains the original rows of A.

answers.label: partial
answers.text: Use eigenvectors as columns of S and eigenvalues in Lambda, but I have not stated the independence condition or the exact factorization.

assessment.subject: Principles of Epidemiology
assessment.question: Define epidemiology and explain what distribution, determinants, and application mean in that definition.
rubric: study of health-related states or events in specified populations
distribution covers frequency and pattern by person place and time
determinants are causes and risk factors
application means using findings to control health problems

answers.label: strong
answers.text: Epidemiology studies the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations and applies that study to control health problems. Distribution asks how often and in what patterns disease occurs by person, place, and time. Determinants are causes and risk factors, and application turns the evidence into public-health action.

answers.label: misconception
answers.text: Epidemiology is the treatment of one sick patient by choosing a drug. Distribution means delivering the medicine and determinants are the patient's appointment times.

answers.label: partial
answers.text: Epidemiology studies disease patterns in populations and tries to find risk factors. It can guide prevention, but I have not explained the formal ideas of distribution and application.

teachback.subject: Machine Learning Reliability

topic_record.name: Data leakage
topic_record.description: Information from held-out data improperly influences model fitting or selection.

teachback.pre_question: A student selects features using the entire dataset and then cross-validates a classifier. Explain the evaluation problem.
teachback.post_question: A student imputes missing values before creating validation folds. Apply the same principle and give a safe workflow.
rubric: fits learned transformations only on training folds
applies the fitted transformation to validation data
teachback.pre_answer: It might be unfair because the classifier sees too many features.
teachback.explanation: Feature selection and imputation learn parameters from data. If they are fitted before the split, held-out samples influence the learned transformation and the validation estimate can become optimistic. Put the transformation and estimator in one pipeline; on every fold, fit the pipeline only on the training fold and transform the validation fold with those fitted parameters.
teachback.post_answer: Imputation learns values such as means, so computing them before the folds lets validation observations influence training. Build a pipeline containing the imputer and model. For each fold fit both only on its training partition, then transform and score its held-out partition.
